clue.text: Girl's not finished eating hot Japanese food

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so one piece is swallowed by another
a thing not finished stops short of its end, so its last letter is missing

parts.note: Susie is a girl's name
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A woman who hasn't finished her meal of spicy Japanese food.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'; the shortened girl's name takes the hot letter inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice topped or rolled with raw fish.

clue.text: Military show inking on skin

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an evening display of military music and marching, like the Edinburgh one
second meaning: a design pricked into the skin with ink

explanation.surface: Soldiers on parade showing off their inked skin.
explanation.walkthrough: The Edinburgh Military Tattoo is a famous annual display of military bands in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an outdoor display of military bands and drill, and a permanent design pricked into the body.

clue.text: Stock a line in fashionable style

indicators.note: a thing placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: ton is a dated word for high fashion or style
L is the abbreviation for line
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shop stocking a range in a trendy style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' looks like shop goods but is the card-game sense: the cards left undealt.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games the talon is the pile of undealt cards from which players draw, also called the stock.

clue.text: Staunch supporter

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to stop a flow, as of blood
second meaning: the stalk that holds up a leaf or flower

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it looks like an adjective and a noun, a loyal fan; split, staunch is a verb meaning to stop a flow.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem bleeding is to check it, and a plant's main stalk props up its leaves and flowers.

clue.text: Returning to identify one's dope

indicators.note: returning means coming back the way one went, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written
to ID someone is the informal verb, shortened from identify, meaning to check who they are
I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Coming back to pick out one person's drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' tempts as drugs, but it means a fool; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is a stupid person, a fool, which is just what calling someone an idiot means.

clue.text: Actually, "nymphet" is misused and not in a kind way

indicators.note: something misused is put to the wrong purpose, so the letters are wrongly ordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pedant pointing out that a certain word is being used wrongly and unkindly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Actually' looks like a sentence opener, but every letter of it is part of the seventeen to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting unsympathetically means showing no compassion or understanding, treating someone harshly.

clue.text: Endlessly prolong situation not having to settle in mitigation

indicators.note: without an end, a word loses its final letter
not having something means being without it, so those letters are removed

parts.note: to extend is to prolong
taken as written
to sit is to settle, as a bird settles on a perch

explanation.surface: A lawyer pleading that a sentence should be cut short because the case won't settle.
explanation.walkthrough: Two words each lose letters: the first its last, the second its opening three.
explanation.definitionFit: Extenuation is the lessening of blame through excusing circumstances, the same as pleading mitigation in court.

clue.text: Middle of Kent county, nice and never one inconvenience

indicators.note: never means not at any point, so a letter is barred from appearing at all
the middle is the centre of a word, so only its central letters are kept

parts.note: the two central letters of the English county
Cumbria is a county in north-west England
taken as written
I is one in Roman numerals, here taken out wherever it occurs

explanation.surface: A traveller finds the drive from the middle of Kent to a pleasant county a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nice' looks like a description of the county; it is just letters. Both the county and that word lose their I.
explanation.definitionFit: An encumbrance is a burden or impediment that gets in the way, causing hindrance and trouble.
